column3: NASB adds “brother.”
NASB follows the critical text (“our sister”). A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “upon my prayers” as “in my prayers.”
NASB renders “hearing” as “because I hear.”
NASB reads “in you,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “in us.” It adds “I pray that” and renders “in Christ” as “for Christ's sake” and “acknowledgment” as “knowledge.”
NASB follows the critical text (“joy … I have”); it renders “I have” as “I have come to have” and “encouragement” as “comfort.”
NASB adds “though” and “to do” and renders “boldness” as “confidence.”
NASB renders “exhort” as “appeal to” and “aged” as “the aged,” and sets the clause off with dashes.
NASB follows the critical text without “my”; “exhort” is rendered “appeal to,” and “chains” is “imprisonment.”
NASB follows the critical text (“both”).
NASB follows the critical text without “receive him”; it adds “that is, sending.”
NASB renders “in the chains of the gospel” as “in my imprisonment for the gospel.”
NASB renders “according to necessity” as “by compulsion” and “according to willingness” as “of your own free will.”
NASB renders “was separated” as “was … parted from you” and “possess” as “have … back.”
NASB renders “above a slave” as “more than a slave.”
NASB renders “receive” as “accept” and adds “you would.”
NASB adds “anything” and renders “charge this to me” as “charge that to my account.”
NASB renders “did write” as “am writing” and puts the aside in parentheses.
NASB follows the critical text (“in Christ”); “I would have profit” is rendered “let me benefit.”
NASB follows the critical text; “having been persuaded” is rendered “Having confidence,” and “above” is “more than.”
NASB renders “I will be granted to you” as “I shall be given to you.”
NASB follows the critical text (“greets”).
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text without “our,” “Amen,” and the Textus Receptus subscription.
